stories.headline: McDavid scoring 200-plus? Devils now Cup-worthy? Wyshynski judges one-month NHL overreactions
stories.summary: With double-digit games in the books for all 32 teams, the hot takes are flying.
stories.body:
The first month of the NHL season should not be ignored, dismissed or hand-waved away.

Sure, there are narratives established quickly that seem a little silly by season's end -- it turns out Vancouver's Paul Cotter might have used up all his goals when he scored four in the first four games of the season, for example. But most of the time, what's happening now is prologue: Six of the eight teams that eventually made the playoffs in the West last season were in playoff spots last Halloween.

Here are 10 overreactions to the happenings on and off the ice to start the 2026-27 NHL season, starting with hockey's most electrifying player trying to do something we haven't seen anyone but Wayne Gretzky do before.

Connor McDavid will break 200 points
It's been interesting to watch the two best centers in the NHL react to their respective playoff disappointments due to injury and lingering angst from accepting Olympic silver.

Nathan MacKinnon decided to start punching people in the face. Connor McDavid decided to break Wayne Gretzky's single-season scoring record of 215 points (1985-86) -- or at least threaten to do so while potentially becoming the only player in NHL history other than Gretzky to score 200 points in a season.

McDavid had 34 points through his first 12 GAMES of the season. That means he outscored Alex Killorn's entire 82-game campaign last season (33 points) with games to spare in October.

The verdict: OVERREACTION. Look, we all want this to happen. It would be incredible for hockey, like an unexpected sequel to Alex Ovechkin breaking Gretzky's career goals record. McDavid is a singular offensive talent in NHL history, with an alchemy of speed and agility and hands and vision and scoring ability that just hasn't existed in a human on skates before. If anyone is going to break Gretzky's record, it's him. If anyone is going to get to 200 points in the modern game, it's him.

McDavid is scoring at a 2.83 points-per-game pace. So, using back of the napkin math, that would be around 204 points added to the 34 he's already scored, which would shatter Gretzky's record like it dipped into liquid nitrogen.

Reasons to believe, beyond "well, it's McDavid": It appears that McDavid and Draisaitl are lineys. McDavid has played just 32 minutes away from Draisaitl this season. When they hired Mike Babcock as head coach -- "they" as in Connor and Leon, not the Oilers -- apparently one of the conditions was that these two megastars wanted to play more on the same line at even strength. While that's not ultimately great for team depth or their postseason conditioning -- McDavid has the highest average ice time of his career so far -- it's hard to argue with the statistical results for Nos. 97 and 29.

Reasons not to believe: It's not the mid-1980s, and the highest point total we've had in this century is McDavid's 153 points in 2022-23, when he played 82 games. Also ... playing 82 games. McDavid did it last season, but has been over 80 games played in just three of the last five seasons. McDavid and Draisaitl haven't both played 80 games or more in the same season since 2022-23.

Again, it would be magical for the NHL if McDavid threatens the record or even 200 points. Breaking records or smashing through stats ceilings is catnip for American sports fans. Of course, I'm a little concerned that the Asterisk Society will come after Connor for having achieved this in an 84-game season. But that would be a good problem to have.

Evan Bouchard will win the Norris Trophy
There's a science to winning the Norris Trophy as the NHL's best defenseman. Players usually have to be in the conversation for a season or two before they break through to win it, like when Bouchard finished fifth for the Norris in 2024 and fourth last season.

Usually, defensemen need a combination of offensive success -- in the last eight full NHL seasons, seven Norris winners had at least 70 points -- and defensive impact, even if it's reputationally. There have been cases made for Bouchard's defensive acumen over the last couple of seasons, but the arguments have yet to crystalize nationally that he's something more than a one-dimensional player.

So perhaps Bouchard has decided to take another road to the Norris that's been successful for others: Offensive dominance that's so overwhelming that his award-worthiness becomes undeniable, like when Erik Karlsson won in 2023 with 101 points and a minus-26, for example.

The verdict: SLIGHT OVERREACTION. Bouchard has 21 points in 12 games, skating to a plus-17. That's the best points-per-game average in the NHL among defensemen (1.75), quite easily. Those stats aren't likely to deflate, given that Bouchard spends copious amounts of time with McDavid and Draisaitl at 5-on-5 and on special teams. If anyone can score his way to the Norris, it's him.

That established: There still needs to be a few more voters willing to accept his defensive competence or at least that the best defense can be a dominating offense. That gets Bouchard from candidate to Norris winner, ultimately.

Connor Hellebuyck makes the New Jersey Devils Cup-worthy
There are two constants during Jack Hughes' career with the Devils: Injuries, and not just the ones he's suffered through; and a lack of consistent, dependable goaltending.

In his previous seven seasons, the Devils ranked no better than 11th in team save percentage and ranked 19th or worse in five of those seasons -- including 30th and 31st overall. Watching the Devils skaters slump their shoulders on the bench as the first shot against of the game flew past their own goalie happened too frequently.

Hellebuyck gives the Devils their best goalie since Martin Brodeur and a last line of defense they've lacked. It's a game-changing trade that takes a good team and potentially makes it great.

The verdict: NOT AN OVERREACTION. Watching Hellebuyck's debut against the Dallas Stars, you could see why he'd waive his trade protection for the Devils. When they're on their game, they possess the puck and limit chances in their own zone. They have a cadre of skill players and a deep blue line, accentuated by the best season of Luke Hughes' career so far. He won't be asked to lug this team to a playoff seed like a tugboat pulled a dilapidated ship. When things are clicking, all he needs to be is the last line of defense.

Again, he takes a good team and elevates it. GM Sunny Mehta had already done good work in building out the team's bottom six, and that work likely continues with Dawson Mercer now in Winnipeg.

I think the East still goes through either Carolina or Florida, but you can already see the confidence in the Devils' game now that their goaltending has been fortified.

The New York Rangers are a playoff team
The Rangers were one of the biggest shocks of the first month of the season, not just for their strong start but for having the start continue through a season-ending injury to goalie Igor Shesterkin. As of Wednesday, they were third in the Metro Division in points, holding down a playoff spot for most of the season.

The verdict: OVERREACTION. OK, it's a tenuous grip on a playoff spot at best. Through Wednesday, the Rangers were fifth in the Metro in points percentage with a goal differential that had dipped to just a plus-2. Rookie goalie Dylan Garand was still holding down the fort, but the Rangers' 5-on-5 numbers in shot share and goal-scoring remain underwater.

There are some absolute bright spots in what might otherwise have been a very dark start for the Rangers, like Adam Fox playing at a Norris Trophy pace and Alexis Lafreniere scoring nine goals in 14 games. But they're starting to wobble right as teams like the Capitals and Islanders are starting to find their footing.

Jacob Fowler will win the Calder Trophy
Give agent Gerry Johannson credit. He managed to get Montreal goalie Jakub Dobes a three-year, $16.07 million contract extension in July (through 2029-30), and his client might be supplanted as Canadiens' starter before the holidays.

Some of that is Dobes being unable to recapture the magic of his regular- and postseason runs for Montreal last season. But most of it is the ascendence of his understudy Fowler, who has been one of the NHL's best goaltenders through seven games: 6-1-0, .942 save percentage, a 1.54 goals-against average and two shutouts. There isn't a rookie goalie close to his stats at the moment. Heck, there might not even be a rookie skater in the same conversation as Fowler at this point.

The verdict: SLIGHT OVERREACTION. Fowler is building an immaculate case right now, but there are a few factors to consider here. The first is Dobes, who built up a lot of good will during Montreal's run to the conference finals. Goaltending success is fickle. One Fowler slump and Dobes groove, and the 25-year-old Czech could get the crease back.

The second is the nature of the Calder Trophy race, which is a typically crowded field. Fowler has netminders such as Dylan Garand (Rangers), Colten Ellis (Sabres) and Sergei Murashov (Penguins) in his rookie class. The race among rookie forwards -- a class that includes Gavin McKenna (Maple Leafs), James Hagens (Bruins), Ivar Stenberg (Sharks) and Porter Martone (Flyers) -- is just getting started. Cole Hutson (Capitals) appears to be the best of the defensemen.

Fowler has planted his flag in this Calder Trophy race, to be sure. But please note that five of the last seven players to win rookie of the month honors in the first month of the season went on to finish outside the top three for the Calder. Of course, the other two were Matthew Schaefer and Moritz Seider, so ...

Simon Edvinsson will be traded before Dylan Larkin
The Detroit Red Wings have made more news off the ice than on the sheet this season. Restricted free agent defenseman Edvinsson has yet to play this season, as he reportedly seeks an exit from Detroit after rejected several contract offers from the team. Captain Larkin rejoined the Red Wings after his request for a trade went public last summer and has six points in 10 games after having the "C" removed from his uniform.

Interim GM Shawn Horcoff hasn't found an offer for either player that's satisfactory for the Red Wings. And so we watch and they wait, for what many believe with be an Edvinsson trade first and foremost.

The verdict: NOT AN OVERREACTION. Edvinsson's situation has something that Larkin's does not, which is a ticking clock. If the 23-year-old blueliner isn't signed by Dec. 1, he'll be ineligible to play in the NHL for the remainder of the 2026-27 season. Obviously, that deadline is significant not only for the Red Wings and their disgruntled player, but also for any teams giving up assets to acquire him.

That alone should have Edvinsson on the move before Larkin. But also consider that Larkin is on the roster and contributing to a team desperate to make the playoffs again; and that the return for a top center needs to be a home run for the Red Wings, which will also delay a Larkin deal.

The Los Angeles Kings are a disaster
When the Kings hired Peter Laviolette in the offseason, it was reasonably assumed that they could extend their playoff appearance streak to six seasons ... even if, at best, the Kings were looking at a sixth straight first-round exit in the Western Conference. Making the playoffs is what Lavy does: His teams have made the cut in his first full season at each of his six previous NHL coaching stops.

But in the first season of the post-Anze Kopitar Era in L.A., that playoff streak appears to already be in serious jeopardy. The Kings were 3-6-2 in their first 11 games, for a .364 points percentage. They had a minus-9 goal differential -- please note that the Kings have only finished in the negative five times in their last 16 seasons.

The verdict: NOT AN OVERREACTION. Kings blogger Alexander Legget of Mayors Manor recently offered this stat: There have been 74 teams in NHL history with a 3-8 record through 11 games. Only 13 of them made the playoffs, or 17.6%. In the last 10 seasons, only four teams out of 28 made the playoff cut. So that's the climb for the Kings.

But the reaction here isn't that Los Angeles will miss the playoffs. It's that they're a disaster, and that's a reasonable take at this juncture, unfortunately. Fears about their offensive depth are confirmed: While the top line of Artemi Panarin, Alex Laferriere and Adrian Kempe has been dominant, the rest of the roster looks anemic. Foundational player Quinton Byfield's breakout season looks to be deferred again. That 30-goal season from Trevor Moore a few years back remains a distant memory. Maybe there's an uptick if and when Kevin Fiala returns, but he's not enough.

There was talk that the Kings were in on Connor Hellebuyck before he was traded to the Devils. That made little sense, but then there hasn't been much lately that's made sense about the Kings' direction. Pity Drew Doughty, loyal to a fault and praying that the Kings could build a contender again in his twilight years. Those prayers aren't going to be answered.

Auston Matthews is a superstar again
Earlier this week, Matthews became the fastest player in Toronto Maple Leafs history to reach 800 career points, needing just 703 games. Darryl Sittler hit 800 in 742 games back in 1980, in an era when points were showered down on every stat sheet like confetti on New Year's Eve.

Of course, it was also a reminder that Matthews had 727 points in his first 629 career games and thus had 74 in his next 71 games -- still impressive, but nowhere near his elite career pace.

Matthews wasn't Matthews over the last two seasons due to injury and roster turnover. His career high of 69 goals in 2023-24 was followed by goal-scoring seasons of 33 and 27 tallies. Was this still a franchise-level superstar that could control play and challenge for MVP honors? He didn't even crack the top 10 in our preseason player ranking on ESPN!

Well, guess what? He has 20 points in 14 games, including nine goals for a 54-goal pace.

The verdict: NOT AN OVERREACTION. Papi's home.

Matthews has been absolutely dominant offensively so far this season, including a 22.5% shooting percentage. Even if that dips, this is a guy who used to top out at around an 18% shooting percentage in his typical seasons.

My colleague Rachel Kryshak made an excellent point in her "One Month Breakouts" article this week: "According to NHL Edge, Matthews has jumped from the 52nd and 72nd percentiles in 20-22 mph and 18-20 mph bursts in 2025-26, to the 68th and 93rd percentiles this season. He has been far more involved off the puck, specifically on the forecheck, resulting in his line forcing turnovers, extending offensive zone time and creating more scoring chances."

First off, elite usage of NHL Edge stats, above their usual application as Jumbotron trivia. Second, that's evidence of a player who is finally healthy and has put in the work in the offseason to get his game back to where it belongs.

San Jose can't meet the hype
Macklin Celebrini's MVP-worthy campaign (45 goals, 115 points) last season had the Sharks just four points away from their first postseason berth since 2019. Hence, they became a popular preseason pick as a breakout team in the Pacific Division, especially after some offseason acquisitions -- defensemen Darnell Nurse, Jacob Trouba and Michael Kesselring, and No. 2 overall pick forward Ivar Stenberg -- deepened their roster.

So far this season, the Sharks' offense hasn't gotten cooking yet beyond another stellar start for Celebrini. One assumes it's just a matter of time before it does. But the systemic problems San Jose has faced defensively -- through 12 games, they were 31st in expected goals against at 5-on-5 -- have continued and could undermine their season.

The verdict: OVERREACTION. Even those who believed the Sharks could make the playoffs didn't expect them to shut down opponents like a mid-90s neutral-zone trap team. The formula for San Jose is essentially the formula for the Anaheim Ducks in their playoff breakthrough last season: Outscore your defensive problems and hope your goaltending holds the fort enough to make the postseason cut.

The Ducks were 29th in goals against per game last season (3.51) and 13th in goals for (3.23), with Lukas Dostal just a bit underwater in goals saved above expected (minus-2.9). The Sharks were 30th in goals against last season (3.54) and 17th in goals for (3.04), with Yaroslav Askarov basically an analytics disaster (minus-18.9).

Through 12 games this season, the Sharks were still defensively porous, if slightly improved (3.50). Askarov and Alex Nedeljkovic have both been on the plus side of goals saved above expected. So there are some early signs that the defense and goaltending might be improving.

Their offense sputtering is unexpected, in the sense that we didn't think a Macklin Celebrini-led team would be scoring at a Calgary Flames pace at 5-on-5 through the first dozen games. This team had a 10.1% shooting percentage at evens last season and came out of the gate this season shooting 6.4%. We still think the hype is real about the black and teal.

Quinn Hughes will not re-sign with Minnesota
The summer came and went without a Hughes extension in Minnesota. Training camp did the same, as did the start of the season. The Norris Trophy winner has been saying the right things to local media about his time with the Wild being "some of the most fun hockey I've ever played" and that "I wouldn't be surprised if something happens soon" regarding his future in Minnesota.

But every day without a contract extension is another day closer to unrestricted free agency next summer, where he could waltz to join brothers Jack and Luke in New Jersey should the Devils want to do in that direction. Former NHLer Ryan Whitney, on a recent episode of "Spittin' Chiclets," went as far as to say that there was a "100% chance" that Quinn plays for the Devils next season.

The verdict: NOT AN OVERREACTION. In full disclosure, the original summation here was more optimistic about Hughes's changes to remain in Minnesota. But then Guerin went on "The Chad Hartman Show" on Wednesday and said:

"I have to just let Quinn do his thing, have his interviews, say what he needs to say. I'm not going to try to get in his head. All I'm doing right now is letting this kid play hockey. He's playing great, he's helping us win games. I've always said that whatever will happen, will happen, and the only person that knows what's going on in Quinn's head is Quinn, and that's OK. I just want to just keep moving forward and winning games."

Alright...

"To be quite honest with you, there's nothing to talk about right now. What am I going to do? Like, going 'please, please, please?' This is a unique situation. Quinn has to wrap his head around a couple of things, and I don't think anything's changed. Right now I'm focused on our team and winning games. Quinn's situation will resolve itself at some point."

Oh ...

"At some point in time, I'll have to try to figure things out and see what's best for the team. But I know one thing's for sure: Having Quinn on our team is what's best for the team. I'll be completely honest with you: I don't know. I don't know what's going to happen. I don't know what I'm going to do. There's no date. What we're doing right now is focusing on our team and trying to win hockey games. That's really it. I think some people want to make this more complicated than it really is, being the media. And it's not that complicated."

Yikes.

Well, I guess there's always the chance he signs in Minnesota just to spite those haters in Vancouver and their chants. There's always a chance.

WINNERS AND LOSERS
Winner: Montreal Canadiens
The Canadiens skate into Manitoba, win the Heritage Classic in front of a giant fake fireplace and wood paneling, and then had Cole Caufield say Montreal "might be Canada's favorite team" based on their fan support. Magnifique!

Loser: Michael Andlauer
I think that Ottawa Senators fans sufficiently rebuked Brady Tkachuk upon his return as a Florida Panther, from the chants in the stands to the totems in the urinals. But in the middle of praising those fans on the "Coming In Hot" podcast, Senators owner Michael Andlauer couldn't leave well enough alone in discussing Tkachuk, his former captain who "found somebody else" after last season. (Andlauer's words.)

The owner shared this anecdote from when Tkachuk opened the scoring for Florida and put Ottawa down a goal. "He skated by our bench and said, 'Some things never change, eh boys?' I don't think that motivated our players much," he said, sarcastically. When you're trying to bury the guy who jilted your franchise, maybe don't make him seem abjectly hilarious.

Winner: Kirill Kaprizov
Here's how the season has started for Wild star Kirill Kaprizov. Offensively, he led the league with 14 goals in 14 games, which puts him on pace to score 84 goals this season, which would be the fifth highest total in NHL history.

Defensively, as analyst Mike Kelly noted, Kaprizov's line with Matt Boldy and Joel Eriksson Ek has the most 5-on-5 ice time together (142:51) this season without having allowed a goal against. Building a pretty good case for "worth the money" for GM Bill Guerin.

Loser: Fun
After Calgary's Matvei Gridin scored his second goal of the game against Toronto on Monday, this 20-year-old hockey player had the AUDACITY to hit the Griddy briefly during his goal celebration. Because that's his nickname and, as he told Sportsnet after the game, he felt it was a good time to breakout the viral dance because the Flames were up three goals and "having fun" in the moment.

As usual, any goal celebration beyond the standard issue received some tired criticism from the old guard. Or as Gridin put it: "A couple old guys said it was a bit too much, but I think they loved it."

Winner: Sunny Mehta's logic
Hey, turns out he doesn't hate goaltenders.

When I interviewed Mehta, we discussed a controversial quote he gave NHL.com about his approach to goaltending: "I'm reluctant to invest significant assets there instead of in areas where the results may be more predictable."

Having given up significant assets for a goaltender, how does he square that philosophy now?

At his news conference last weekend, Mehta referenced a paper he wrote in 2010 in which he "built a Bayesian hierarchical model where I show you exactly what I think the talent distribution is among goaltenders." At the time, Roberto Luongo as at the top of the chart. The spread between elite goalies and the rank and file is "narrower than most people think, but that doesn't mean the spread is zero at all" he said. But in the case of Hellebuyck, the trade was in keeping with his research and his recent quote.

"If the goaltending position is tricky to predict, where do you want to bet on? You want to bet on a person with a large sample size of excellent results who's on a good cap hit. To me, this is exactly congruent with that," he said.

I mean, if you have a Bayesian hierarchical model that proves otherwise, be my guest ...

Loser: Canadian Exceptionalism
The exodus of American players from Canada has reignited an extremely tiresome viewpoint that winning in a Canadian market is more meaningful than doing the same in a U.S. market. Bryan Hayes of the TSN Overdrive show was the latest peddler of this exhaustion, in reference to Connor Hellebuyck moving from Winnipeg to a less "pressure-filled" market in Jersey:

"Maybe I'm romanticizing it too much but playing in a packed building with fans that live and die by it, that are going to remember you forever, where unfortunately there are a lot of other markets in the U.S. where that's not applicable. There are too many players running from it."

Moving past the absurd notion that American hockey fans aren't equipped to "live and die" by their teams because they're not Canadian, the Stanley Cup weighs the same no matter where you lift it. And sorry, but the Flyer who brings the first championship to Philadelphia since 1975 will be as legendary as Mark Messier ending a 54-year drought in New York or Sidney Crosby winning three Cups in Pittsburgh or even the Golden Misfits who lifted Stanley in the Nevada desert for the first time.

Or, you know, the American goalie who made 41 saves in an Olympic gold medal game recently ...

FAVORITE ON-ICE MOMENT

Detroit Red Wings rookie Michal Postava made his first NHL start against the Edmonton Oilers this week, and all he had to do for his first NHL win was make a game-saving stop on Evan Bouchard at the end of overtime and then make saves on Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins in the shootout.

Some victories are given. Some are earned.

FAVORITE OFF-ICE MOMENT

Halloween is a joyous time in the NHL. Some costumes were obvious, like Macklin "Maverick" Celebrini and wingman Will "Goose" Smith. (Will, please do not look up what happens to Goose.)

Some were less expected, like Erik Karlsson dressing up as a Fem-Bot from "Austin Powers." What a way to celebrate the 10th anniversary of his iconic "Black Swan" costume.

JERSEY FOUL OF THE WEEK

The return of Quinn Hughes to Vancouver produced a treasure trove of Jersey Fouls, many of them unpublishable.

This "Quit Hughes" one sent by Nate Weigel was Wysh List-friendly. Alas, we couldn't find a good look at the Jersey Foul where a Canucks fan doctored the nameplate to say "UGH."

MUST-SEE GAMES

Columbus Blue Jackets at Dallas Stars

Saturday, Oct. 31, 8 p.m. ET | ESPN+

Zach Werenski makes his first visit to Dallas after rejecting a trade to the Stars during the offseason. Multiple reports at the time said that Dallas defenseman Thomas Harley would have been sent back to the Jackets, in a trade many anticipate could be revisited some day down the line. Nothing awkward about any of this!

Edmonton Oilers at New Jersey Devils

Tuesday, Nov. 3, 7:30 p.m. ET | ESPN+/Disney+/Hulu

It's the Connor vs. Connor matchup we all want to see. McDavid threatening NHL scoring records. Hellebuyck likely making his first home start in New Jersey as a member of the Devils. Obviously this is the thing that all of the United States will be focused on next Tuesday night.

PUCK HEADLINES
DATELINE: Hellebuyck Trade
One more note on the Hellebuyck trade drama. KSL Sports reporter Cole Bagley caused a stir when he said the Jets asked the Mammoth for either Logan Cooley or Dylan Guenther in a Hellebuyck deal.

Multiple sources have told me this is the level of player GM Kevin Cheveldayoff was seeking, not only from Utah but from another Hellebuyck suitor in the Carolina Hurricanes, where the ask was for either Logan Stankoven or Seth Jarvis.

Obviously, these were all nonstarters. The problem for Utah, Carolina and other potential trade partners was that they didn't have a "next best option" forward that could entice Winnipeg. The Devils had one in Dawson Mercer -- 25 years old, no trade protection, two controllable seasons and one assumes some level of assurance that he'll remain in Winnipeg -- along with 2026 12th overall pick Alexander Command, a player Cheveldayoff had on his draft board too.

DATELINE: St. Louis

I still can't believe this is real: The Blues are giving away an Ozzy Osbourne bobblehead to the first 10,000 fans on Dec. 2, a statue honoring one of the most iconic mugshots in NHL history.

The year was 1984. Ozzy was on his "Bark At The Moon" tour. He played St. Louis and somehow came into possession of a Blues shirt that he would wear 12 days later while "staggering drunk" on Beale Street in Memphis, where he was booked on one misdemeanor count of public intoxication.

For years, the Blues allowed a cottage industry of shirts and other trinkets featuring the mugshot to thrive. They finally embraced the Ozzy of it all during their 2019 Stanley Cup run, as Ozzy tweeted a photo of himself in a decidedly different Blues sweater.

Kudos to whoever hopped on the Crazy Train and cooked up this bobblehead.

stories.headline: Fantasy basketball: Seven preseason assumptions already being challenged
stories.summary: The fantasy basketball experts go over what hasn't gone as planned during the opening week of the NBA season.
stories.body:
Sometimes, it takes a while to see how the things are going to shake out in this new NBA season. Other times, it is plainly obvious that things are not as they seemed before the season officially tipped off, whether that means less playing time, a drop in production, or changes under a new coaching staff.

With that in mind, we asked our fantasy basketball experts Andre Snellings, Eric Moody, Eric Karabell, Steve Alexander, Jim McCormick and Michael F. Florio to identify the biggest preseason assumptions that are already being challenged.

Here's what has stood out to them after one week of NBA action.

Tyrese Maxey, other 76ers thriving despite Philadelphia's star power

Moody: The concern in Philadelphia was that too many stars would eat into Maxey's production. LeBron James and Jaylen Brown joined Joel Embiid, but Maxey averaged 50 fantasy points per game through four games as the Sixers opened 3-1. Brown contributed 36.0 fantasy points per game, and Embiid recorded a 28-point triple-double against the Milwaukee Bucks last Saturday. There will be nights when someone sacrifices touches, but Maxey hasn't looked like the player making that sacrifice.

Florio: While LeBron and Embiid have already missed a game and that was a big fear, they have performed extremely well so far, especially in Roto formats. Maxey is a Top 5 player in all formats, while Embiid and Brown are each averaging over 20 PPG. LeBron James continues to contribute across the board. It's still early, but fading them in fantasy is one early season regret.

Giannis' arrival is already affecting Adebayo's production
Karabell: Perhaps I hadn't considered the potential statistical downside of what superstar Giannis Antetokoumpo joining the Miami Heat would mean for longtime underrated star Bam Adebayo. So far, the fit looks awkward. Adebayo averaged 20.1 PPG and 10 RPG last season, continuing a seven-season run of excellence. Is that over now? Bam is off to a terrible start (11.8 PPG, 7.3 RPG, 40% FG, 61.5% FT), and oh, Miami is winless. These numbers must improve, but how much? Is Bam still a top 50 fantasy option? Maybe so, maybe not.

Alex Sarr will have to wait to reach new heights
Snellings: Sarr is unlikely to approach, let alone build on, his breakout campaign from last season if the Washington Wizards are fully healthy. After averaging 16.3 PPG, 7.4 RPG and 2.0 BPG last season, he is currently averaging 8.8 PPG, 5.3 RPG and 1.3 BPG in this one. With Anthony Davis occupying all the spaces Sarr prefers but at much higher volume, Sarr just doesn't have the shots (6.5 FGA this season, down from 13.7 FGA last year), rebounding or shot-blocking opportunities to approach what he did last season. And number one overall pick AJ Dybantsa hasn't even played yet this season, so once he's in the fold Sarr may get even fewer looks.

Jabari Smith Jr. is showing signs of another leap

McCormick: I was under the impression that Smith had plateaued as an NBA contributor. It's easy to forget Smith was the No. 3 overall pick in his 2022 draft class, with a prospect profile that hinted at potentially special 3-and-D potential. The defense has been impressive and improving throughout, while the offensive side of his game appeared stagnant over recent seasons. With a real spike in 3-point volume this season, Smith's growth as a multi-level scorer is a key factor in Houston's potential to enter the contending class. In fantasy terms, Smith is a solid player to target, as this ascent appears sustainable.

Nikola Vucevic fantasy role is shrinking
Snellings: Vucevic's run of consistent fantasy production appears to be over. He rejoined the Orlando Magic this offseason, and the thought was that he would battle Wendell Carter Jr. for minutes and production at center. Instead, thus far Carter is averaging 30.7 minutes per game versus Vucevic's 8.0 MPG. And Carter is off to a great start, arguably the best of his career. Add in that, at age 27, Carter fits on the career arc of the other Magic stars (Paolo Banchero: age 23, Franz Wagner age 25, Desmond Bane age 28) much better than the 36 year-old Vucevic. Barring injury, it's hard to imagine Vucevic's role expanding into fantasy relevance this season.
Early injuries are already testing fantasy managers
Alexander: I came into this season fully aware of how many NBA players deal with injuries and missed games, but I don't think I was prepared for what we saw in Week 1. Anthony Edwards, Jalen Williams, Jaren Jackson Jr., Kawhi Leonard, Cason Wallace, Lauri Markkanen, Kristaps Porzingis, Kon Knueppel, Ivica Zubac and Yves Missi are all out with major injuries and some of them may not even play again this season. Fantasy managers are going to have to make some tough drop/hold decisions going forward, and we still have 24 weeks to go.

stories.headline: Mexico City Grand Prix 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions
stories.summary: Formula 1 heads to Mexico on a weekend where Kimi Antonelli could win the drivers' championship for the first time.
stories.body:
Formula 1 heads to Mexico on a weekend where Kimi Antonelli could win the drivers' championship for the first time.

The Mercedes driver extended his lead in the title to 123 points from George Russell after winning the United States Grand Prix. He will simply need to finish ninth or higher in Mexico City to seal the title.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc was looking strong in the upgraded Ferrari to finish second in Austin, with Max Verstappen on the final step of the podium.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the 19th round.

- F1 readies Antonelli's title champagne in Austin: 'The race of a champion who isn't champion yet'

- How Kimi Antonelli can win F1 title at Mexico GP -- with or without Qatar, Abu Dhabi races

- George Russell: Finishing second in F1 title race 'doesn't mean anything'

Mexico City Grand Prix schedule
All times in GMT

Friday, October 30

Practice One: 6.30 p.m. - 7.30 p.m.

Practice Two: 10 p.m. - 11 p.m.

Saturday, October 31

Final Practice: 5.30 p.m. - 6.30 p.m.

Qualifying: 9 p.m. - 10 p.m.

Sunday, November 1

Mexico Grand Prix: 8 p.m.

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Mexico City Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez
Mexico City is one of the most vibrant atmospheres on the calendar and fans congregate in the thousands to cheer on home hero Sergio Pérez.

It's a true anomaly on the calendar due to the high altitude of of 7,300 feet (2,200 metres) and therefore presents a unique challenge for the teams and drivers. Teams can run Monaco-level downforce packages while still reaching Monza-esque top speeds.

One of the iconic parts of the track -- the Foro Sol stadium section -- includes two tight corners in a former baseball stadium.

Mexico City Grand Prix

Circuit: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez; Mexico City, Mexico

Previous winners in Mexico

2015: Nico Rosberg (Mercedes)

2016: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2017: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

2018: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

2019: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2021: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

2022: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

2023: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

2024: Carlos Sainz (Ferrari)

2025: Lando Norris (McLaren)

Other key stats

First F1 race: 1963

Laps: 71 laps of 4.3km

Lap record: 1:17.774, Valtteri Bottas (2021)

Most wins: Verstappen with five (2017-2018, 2021-2023). Other winners from the current grid are Hamilton (2016, 2019), Sainz (2024) and Norris (2025).

Most poles: Jim Clark with four (1963-1965, 1967). Other pole sitters from the current grid are Hamilton (2016), Leclerc (2019, 2023), Verstappen (2022), Sainz (2024) and Norris (2025).

Weather forecast

The weather for the Mexico City Grand Prix is set to reach temperatures of 27°C for qualifying and Sunday's race, with no rain due.

What happened last time out?
Norris pulled out a thrilling lap to take pole position in Mexico, his first pole since the Belgian Grand Prix in July. The Brit said on the team radio afterwards "What a lap. What a lap. Even I don't know how I did that."

It was a dominant race weekend from the McLaren driver after he became the new leader in the title race ahead of his teammate Oscar Piastri for the first time since April.

He had a one point advantage over Piastri with just four races to go.

Who will win this year?

Antonelli put his Mercedes on a surprise pole in Austin and converted it into another victory as he inches closer to taking the title crown with five races remaining.

The youngster will need just two points this weekend, or for Russell and Hamilton to not win the race, to get the job done in Mexico.

Red Bull are a looming threat each weekend after bringing major upgrades and Verstappen will be one to watch out for. He's also got five race victories under his belt around Mexico City.

All eyes will be on Antonelli. He will be hoping to wrap up the title and is looking like he's in a position where nobody will be able to stop him.

stories.headline: Power to burn and a 'trademark' goal: why Ethan Drever has rocketed up draft boards
stories.summary: Growing up an Essendon supporter, Ethan Drever hasn't 'seen anything' like success. But his rise up draft boards could have him in the frame to be his childhood club's first pick, writes Jasper Chellappah.
stories.body:
Ethan Drever had absolutely no choice on his AFL team. As a newborn he was put in an Essendon jumper at the hospital and he's been a Bomber ever since.

It's been a rough 18 years of fandom since, and he's got some thoughts about his dad's decision.

"I'm [born in] 2008, I haven't seen anything!" he tells ESPN with a grin - and a grimace.

"Dad tells me about his success and I'm like, 'You don't have to rub it in like that.'"

The Dons are entering a new era in 2027 under Mark McVeigh and it's being driven through the draft. They snagged Sullivan Robey, Jacob Farrow, and Dyson Sharp in the first round 12 months ago and now own pick 1 in the upcoming draft.

Drever also has a lot of thoughts about those drafted before him.

"They've got some good young boys in there now. Robey, Sharp, they're gonna be so good.

"I like Farrow. He should be kicking in and doing all that, he needs to be in priority positions. That's what he's gonna be doing in the future.

"Just that halfback, I reckon he's gonna be really good... he's a beautiful left foot kick."

After a dour two-win season the Bombers have first call on Drever, with the 188cm on-baller strongly linked at the top of the board.

He's an electric runner with the intent to tackle, chase, and pressure - something that hasn't been a trait of Essendon's list for a long time.

Asked what he thinks when watching his boyhood club each weekend, Drever's response would prick the ears of all Bombers fans.

"It'd be nice to be out there and sort of help the boys out, that's kinda what I'm thinking!"

The Vic Country MVP and Rebels best and fairest produced a remarkable season. His star has risen from a first-round chance to the very top of the open pool.

He may have the most translatable traits to AFL level of any prospect. Drever is an elite power athlete, recording a 2.92 second 20 metre sprint which comes across in the tape. He bursts out of the contest with driving legs and loves to exit forward of the stoppage to inflict maximum damage.

His ultra consistent season has come about without any injury concerns, something all other top prospects this year haven't been able to say.

"It's been good not to have to sit on the sidelines this year at all and I can just keep playing consistent footy," he says.

"I only missed one [game] which was just after champs, I just had a break."

Drever lays claim to a pretty handy trademark. On six separate occasions this season he's collected the ball -- either out of a stoppage or in open play -- and powered away from opponents into the forward half of the ground.

From there his long running gait and elite top speed helps him separate from chasing defenders and break the paint of 50 to drive home sensational goals.

"I have heard it's called the trademark goal now. I don't know where that's really come from, it's just a natural thing I guess. I just like to run and have a ping from outside 50," Drever tells ESPN.

"Definitely one of my traits is just my power, especially this year. Building up over the pre-season and definitely my two-way running.

"It's the long-term goal to move into the midfield and be a bit of a Jordan Dawson with his two-way running. I love Finn Callaghan, how he plays. Those two are really great role models for me.

"I think Hugh McCluggage as well, I've watched him a lot. I had a meeting with him this year, he's that sort of two-way runner as well and he's been really good for me."

Drever played 13 games for the Rebels this year in amongst commitments with the AFL Academy and Vic Country. He collected the ball 28 times to go with a goal a game, but he's not satisfied with just being an offensive weapon.

The Ballarat local is a tenacious presence in contests with the appetite to chase and tackle, racking up 6.5 per outing to frank his status as the best pure midfielder in the open pool.

At the draft combine he showed off a much-improved engine running a 6:27 minute 2km after going 20 seconds slower in the lead-up. It's a time that will put him towards the front of the pack on day one of pre-season.

Drever knows exactly what's required to be a midfielder at the next level, and he's determined to get there as soon as possible.

"My endurance side was a big goal of mine, obviously at the top level you've just got to be able to run all day.

"Honing in on my fundamentals and trying to get them the best I can as well. That's what the most important thing is because it's the little one percenters that make a difference in the AFL.

Drever is now on the precipice of living out his dream of becoming an AFL player, and it could be for his boyhood club as the top choice in the open pool of the draft.

That won't matter to him, so long as he gets his opportunity to shine on the big stage.

"I don't really care [if I go at pick 1]. It's nice to have my name up in consideration alongside those boys but I'll just be happy to be picked up wherever I go."

stories.headline: Salkilld, Saint Denis to headline UFC Fight Night in Sydney
stories.summary: West Australian Quillan Salkilld will headline a UFC Fight Night lightweight matchup with Benoît Saint Denis in Sydney in February.
stories.body:
West Australian Quillan Salkilld will return to the Octagon in Sydney, after it was confirmed he'll headline the UFC Fight Night with a lightweight bout against Frenchman Benoît Saint Denis on February 7 (AEDT).

Salkilld, 26, is a former Australian rules footballer who turned to MMA after leaving school at 16, and boasts an impressive 13-1 professional record (6-0 in UFC) with five 'performance of the night' bonuses.

The Broome native has won four consecutive fights with a first-round finish, most recently submitting Mateusz Gamrot in their UFC Fight Night clash in Perth in August. He's widely regarded as Australia's next big combat star.

Meanwhile Saint Denis, 30, is one of the lightweight division's most dangerous finishers, and has a 17-4 professional record.

Peter Kloczko, senior vice president of UFC Australia and New Zealand, said the Fight Night -- to take place at Sydney's Afterpay Arena -- would be an "unforgettable event" featuring one of Australia's brightest young stars.

"UFC Fight Night Sydney is set to be another huge moment for Australian fans, and Quillan Salkilld versus Benoît Saint Denis is a main event that delivers everything we look for in this sport," he said in the official release.

"Quillan has been one of the breakout stars of the UFC's lightweight division, while Benoît is one of the most dangerous and exciting finishers in the sport. Bringing this fight to Sydney will make for an unforgettable night."

Further fights on the card will be released in due course.

stories.headline: Kane's long road to Ballon d'Or glory ends with his crowning moment
stories.summary: After a remarkable year for Bayern Munich and England, Harry Kane becoming the world's best player is the ultimate reward for years of perseverance.
stories.body:
LONDON -- It is nine years since Harry Kane lingered at the back of the London Palladium at the end of a soccer awards show.

The Best FIFA Football Awards in 2017 had just concluded with Cristiano Ronaldo handed the men's top prize in addition to leading a team of the year including Lionel Messi, Neymar, Sergio Ramos and Gianluigi Buffon.

As the audience filed out and a few mere mortals loitered in the hope of a selfie, Kane stood near the exit, casting a longing stare at the winners on stage. He has dreamed all his life of being in their place, considered in the same breath as the game's greats.

On Monday, at the same storied West End venue, about nine miles from his birthplace in Leytonstone, he finally is. Sat next to Lamine Yamal with last year's winner Rodri one place further away, Kane kept company with the elite. And then he joined them.

Last week in Munich, he told reporters he had found the wait to learn the winner "very stressful" for himself and his family. The final few hours on Monday won't have helped. The rain present earlier in the day subsided, but the controversy did not.

Less than three hours before the ceremony was due to start, the official website published a profile of Kane as the 2026 Ballon d'Or winner. Alongside one for Kylian Mbappé and one for Yamal. They were swiftly deleted. The entire ceremony was then delayed by 45 minutes with no official reason given, amid some speculation that the notorious London traffic was responsible.

Kane won on the undercard -- the Gerd Müller Men's Award or the Striker of the Year -- to cheers from the locals in the audience. The raucous reaction from the cheap seats before addressing the crowd was a prelude to what followed. It was palpably welcome but not, by itself, an indication of the big one: Striker of the Year is not decided by vote but simply by goals, and Kane's 73 was the best in the men's game.

Having waited for over a decade to live this moment, a few extra minutes made no difference in the end.

"Wow, wow, wow," he said after taking the stage before thanking Tottenham Hotspur by saying "I wouldn't be where I am without you" in a moment of typical class.

Monday's Ballon d'Or triumph is the crowning moment for a player whose story of relentless professionalism and determined aspiration serves as an exemplar for any young player. British media is often criticized for prematurely building up players to an impossible level, only to then knock them down when that level is inevitably never reached.

Kane has always been a different case. He publicly judged himself against Ronaldo and Messi, two of the best in history, and used their devastating consistency as a target to match.

His numbers since joining Bayern Munich are staggering: 158 goals in 156 matches following a €120 million move from Tottenham in 2023. The Ballon d'Or voting period takes into account August 2025 to the end of the World Cup in July.

He scored 73 goals in 65 matches during that period, won the Bundesliga, the DFB-Pokal, the German Supercup and led England to their best FIFA World Cup finish in 60 years with third place, scoring six times at the tournament.

Back in 2017, "The Best" awards were a competition set up by FIFA as a rival to the Ballon d'Or after five years of partnership with organizers France Football had come to an end. Kane was on the 24-man shortlist for Best Men's Player that year. He finished 24th. Of course, his journey to the summit began much further back.

Coming through the Spurs academy, a young Kane had loan spells at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich City and Leicester City, where you would find it extremely difficult to locate anyone honest who genuinely believed at the time they were in the presence of a future world-class talent. A nice kid, sure, a hard worker with a future in the game. But one of England's greatest?

Kane broke into Spurs' first team toward the end of the 2013-14 season and a year later was named PFA Young Player of the Year aged 21, making his England debut in the same season. He marked that moment against Lithuania with a goal then, too.

Fame was a novelty at this point. During a Tottenham preseason tour to Sydney, Kane innocently ventured out to a shopping center in his downtime. He was quickly mobbed by so many adoring fans that the club had to scramble a minibus to bring him back to the team hotel.

Kane went on to score 280 goals in 435 appearances for Spurs while breaking Wayne Rooney's all-time goal-scoring record for England. Barring injury, he will break Peter Shilton's appearance record of 125 caps next month, too.

There was, though, perhaps a sense in the buildup that Kane was not quite the global superstar his Ballon d'Or rivals were, most obviously Messi and Mbappé but also, despite his teenage years, Yamal, named Young Talent of the Year for the third consecutive year.

Former Spurs boss Jose Mourinho alluded to this in a conversation with Kane captured by Amazon in their "All or Nothing" series covering the 2019-20 campaign.

"The world looks to English football with an incredible respect but they still think that the movie stars of football belong to other places -- and I think we have to build also your status in that direction," he said.

Kane replied: "That's my aim. When you are at a club like Tottenham, of course we've done well, personally I've done well, but I want to be Ronaldo, Messi ..."

There he goes again. The Ballon d'Or is voted for by one journalist per country of FIFA's top 100 ranked nations, which brings a different dynamic than, say, the FIFA equivalent, which adds votes from national managers and captains.

He had never finished higher than 10th in the Ballon d'Or vote (2024). There are three criteria, listed in order of importance: individual performances, decisive and impressive character; collective performances and titles won; class and fair play.

And despite the Premier League being one of the United Kingdom's most successful global exports, English players have only ever won it five times (Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton and Kevin Keegan twice) and nobody has triumphed since Michael Owen in 2001.

That's more than two decades of unprecedented growth for the Premier League, and yet LaLiga often feels as though it is where the true individual talents reside. Players from Real Madrid and Barcelona have won it 12 times each. Manchester United are the most successful English club in Ballon d'Or history with four.

Kane, of course, left England in pursuit of silverware after a decade of personal achievement but collective frustration at Spurs. In doing so, he has ended up landing both silverware with Bayern and now the highest individual honor a player can attain.

"I am almost speechless," he said. "Being here in London has made it extra special. It made it a good omen for me tonight." Where once he stared at the Palladium stage, now all eyes are on him.

stories.headline: NRL transfer whispers: Flegler move likely; Cowboys keen to keep Nanai
stories.summary: The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1. Isaac Issa has news from the Dragons on some key outside backs
stories.body:
The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1, with clubs beginning to shape their rosters for 2027 and beyond.

From player movement to changes behind the scenes, ESPN NRL Insider Isaac Issa has the latest whispers from around the competition.

Flegler move looking likely
Tom Flegler is looking likely to leave the Dolphins at the end of 2027, with ESPN understanding the prop is leaning towards a move away from the club.

While Flegler is yet to make a firm decision, the Dolphins are now facing the prospect of losing him for the 2028 season and beyond.

His future shapes as a situation to watch as the November 1 contracting window approaches.

Cowboys keen to keep Nanai
North Queensland remain keen to retain Jeremiah Nanai, with ESPN understanding the Cowboys are hopeful the back-rower will extend his stay despite preparing to test his value on the open market from November 1.

Nanai has been with the club since he was a teenager, developing into a Queensland Origin representative, and the Cowboys are hopeful that connection will help keep him in Townsville.

Samrani expected to test open market
Jordan Samrani is expected to test the open market from November 1. ESPN understands he will explore his options for 2028 and beyond.

Following a breakout season with the Parramatta Eels, Samrani is open to assessing opportunities elsewhere when the contracting window opens on Sunday.

Cochrane set to link up with Titans feeder

Taye Cochrane is set to link up with Gold Coast Titans feeder club Ipswich Jets for the 2027 season following his departure from Canterbury.

ESPN understands the young fullback has signed with the Queensland Cup outfit after the Bulldogs opted against offering him a contract for next season.

Cochrane scored six tries in 14 NSW Cup appearances for Canterbury in 2026, having been part of the club's Jersey Flegg premiership-winning side in 2024.

The move follows Phil Gould's confirmation that Cochrane would leave the Bulldogs, with ESPN revealing he had not been offered a new deal.

Bulldogs opt against Cochrane deal

Canterbury have opted against offering Taye Cochrane a contract for 2027, with the young fullback set to depart Belmore.

ESPN understands Cochrane was not offered a new deal, following Phil Gould's confirmation he would not remain at the Bulldogs next season.

Cochrane scored six tries in 14 NSW Cup appearances this year, playing predominantly at fullback.

He was part of Canterbury's 2024 Jersey Flegg premiership-winning side before progressing to NSW Cup the following season.

Panthers make retention intentions clear on Patea
Penrith have informed Luron Patea's management of their desire to retain the young prop beyond 2027, although he still intends to test the open market from November 1.

ESPN understands multiple clubs are interested in speaking to Patea, who is approaching the final year of his Panthers contract.

ESPN previously reported that Penrith had yet to begin extension discussions with Patea.

Tigers keen to retain Mason

Wests Tigers are keen to retain Heath Mason, with the club working through roster space to accommodate the young utility.

ESPN understands Mason remains part of the Tigers' long-term plans, although his future is yet to be resolved ahead of 2027.

Cowboys open to keeping Taumalolo

North Queensland are open to retaining Jason Taumalolo beyond 2027, with the veteran forward's assessment of how his body is holding up set to guide the next step.

ESPN understands the Cowboys will take their lead from Taumalolo as he weighs up his playing future, reflecting his standing as a club legend.

Taumalolo is contracted until the end of next season and becomes eligible to negotiate with rival clubs for 2028 onwards from November 1.

Panthers lock in Patea
Penrith have secured Tua Patea until the end of 2029, with the youngster signing an extension that includes a pathway from a development contract into the club's top 30.

Patea capped off the 2026 season with a hat-trick in the Panthers' Jersey Flegg Grand Final victory, having started the year with an NRL training block.

The new deal will see him join Penrith's full-time NRL squad as he works towards a first-grade debut.

Bulldogs closing in on Skelton return

Jeral Skelton is closing in on a return to Canterbury following his departure from the Wests Tigers.

ESPN understands the Bulldogs are in advanced discussions to bring the outside back to the club for the 2027 season.

An agreement is understood to be close, although the deal has yet to be finalised.

Multiple NRL sides eye Knights forward

A Sydney club and a Queensland-based club are monitoring Newcastle forward Mat Croker ahead of November 1.

ESPN understands the two clubs have shown interest in the 27-year-old, who is approaching the final year of his Knights contract and can negotiate with rivals for 2028 onwards from next month.

Rivals keeping tabs on Dragons' Tu

Multiple clubs are monitoring St George Illawarra outside back Setu Tu, with the Dragons yet to begin talks over a contract extension.

Tu is contracted until the end of 2027 and is expected to test the open market from November 1, when rival clubs can negotiate a deal for 2028 and beyond.

The former Warriors outside back joined the Dragons on a development contract this season and is set to move into the club's top 30 squad in 2027.

His ability to cover multiple positions across the backline adds to his appeal as clubs assess their recruitment options.

Roosters eye Dockar-Clay reunion
The Roosters have shown interest in a potential return for Zach Dockar-Clay as they explore options to bolster their hooking and utility depth.

ESPN understands the 31-year-old has emerged as an option following his departure from Manly, with discussions remaining at an early stage.

Dockar-Clay spent the 2024 and 2025 seasons with the Roosters before joining the Sea Eagles on a one-year deal for 2026.

Manly confirmed his departure last month after a season in which he claimed the club's NSW Cup best-and-fairest award.

Bostock brushes Dragons links

Dolphins star Jack Bostock has dismissed recent links between himself and the Dragons, admitting this isn't the first time he'd been floated for a club switch.

"I've been linked to a few a clubs," Bostock admitted.

"I don't know about [the Dragons links]."

He said that while he "obviously sees it in the media," his sole focus is the Kangaroos.

Sloan's Dragons stay still a possibility

Tyrell Sloan could yet remain at St George Illawarra next season, with discussions ongoing over a potential stay despite his planned move to Castleford.

There is interest in keeping Sloan at the Dragons, but several hurdles remain before that can become a reality.

Roster space and salary cap room would need to be worked through, while any arrangement would also require Castleford to agree to release him.

Sloan previously admitted he would "love to" remain in the NRL when speaking to Channel Nine in August, after his Castleford deal had been announced.

No agreement has been reached and a stay is far from guaranteed.
